questions.question: In Agile development, what is the primary approach to software delivery?
answers: A. Delivering all functionality at the end of the project.
B. Incrementally building software from the start of the project.
C. Prioritizing user stories in one large cycle.
D. Completing software delivery all at once near the end.

questions.question: What is the role of user stories in Agile development?
answers: A. To serve as documentation for stakeholders.
B. To define the project scope.
C. To prioritize tasks for developers.
D. To represent little bits of user functionality in projects.

questions.question: How does Agile handle project priorities?
answers: A. Completing tasks in a random order.
B. Following a strict sequential plan.
C. Prioritizing user stories based on customer input.
D. Avoiding the need for prioritization.

questions.question: In Agile development, what happens if there is too much to do and not enough time?
answers: A. Prioritize and cut scope (recommended).
B. Extend the project deadline.
C. Decrease the quality of the delivered product.
D. Request more resources.

questions.question: What is one of the benefits of Software Requirements Specification (SRS)?
answers: A. Increasing development effort.
B. Reducing the basis for agreement.
C. Establishing the basis for agreement between customers and suppliers.
D. Eliminating the need for validation.

questions.question: What does SRS provide as a baseline?
answers: A. A basis for increasing costs.
B. A baseline for reducing schedules.
C. A baseline for validation and verification.
D. A basis for decreasing enhancement.

questions.question: What is one of the roles of IEEE?
answers: A. Advocating for reduced technological excellence.
B. Advancing innovation and technological excellence.
C. Limiting access to global community resources.
D. Ignoring the development of technology standards.

questions.question: How many IEEE members are there globally?
answers: A. Less than 100,000.
B. Around 200,000.
C. More than 430,000.
D. Exactly 500,000.

questions.question: Who is responsible for documenting the survey during the System Requirement Review (SRR)?
answers: A. Survey Manager.
B. Survey Presenter.
C. Survey Reviewer.
D. Survey Team Size.

questions.question: What is the recommended team size for the System Requirement Review (SRR)?
answers: A. 1-3 members.
B. 3-7 members.
C. 7-15 members.
D. 15 members or more.

questions.question: Which type of errors are challenging to identify in requirement specifications?
answers: A. Missing requirements.
B. Clearly described general requirements.
C. Partial requirements.
D. Comprehensive functional requirements.

questions.question: Why are partial requirements considered challenging to identify?
answers: A. Because they are comprehensive.
B. Because they cover specific functionalities.
C. Because they lack a full description of required functionality.
D. Because they are always clearly stated.

questions.question: What is a design pattern?
answers: A. A single solution to a design problem.
B. A set of rules for designing objects.
C. A decision-making process for designers.
D. A documented entry with a recognized solution to a design problem.

questions.question: What is the intent of the Factory Method Pattern?
answers: A. To define an interface for creating objects.
B. To retain control of class instantiation.
C. To encapsulate object creation code on the client side.
D. All of the above.

questions.question: How does the Factory Design pattern relate to encapsulation?
answers: A. It avoids encapsulation.
B. It ignores encapsulation principles.
C. It encapsulates object creation code inside a Factory method.
D. It relies on client-side encapsulation.

questions.question: In the Observer pattern, what is the common example provided in graphical user interfaces?
answers: A. Creating objects sequentially.
B. Encapsulating object creation code.
C. Notifying objects when another object changes.
D. Accessing elements of a collection.

questions.question: What is a Test Case in the context of software testing?
answers: A. A piece of code that executes specific functionality.
B. A document describing the approach for software development.
C. A unique identification number for software applications.
D. A document describing how testing will be performed for a specific application.

questions.question: What information should be included in a Test Case document?
answers: A. Test Case Id, Test Description, and Test Steps.
B. Organization name, Test Case Owner, and Creation Date.
C. Test Steps, Expected Value, and Result.
D. All of the above.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Expected Value' field in a Test Case document?
answers: A. To specify the code changes.
B. To document the ideal value for the test case.
C. To record the steps to execute the test case.
D. To identify the owner of the test case.

questions.question: In Unit Testing, what is the main purpose of a unit test?
answers: A. To execute specific functionality in the code under test.
B. To validate the creation date of the test case.
C. To mix normal code with test code.
D. To create a unique identification number for software applications.

questions.question: What is Git primarily used for in the context of version control?
answers: A. Managing local directories.
B. Synchronizing repositories on a server.
C. Organizing files on your local machine.
D. Keeping track of the history of commits.

questions.question: How does Git handle synchronization between different machines?
answers: A. Automatically uploads changes to a central server.
B. Manually copying files between machines.
C. Synchronizing with the server to pick up changes.
D. Ignoring changes when moving between machines.

questions.question: What advantage does Git provide in terms of commit history?
answers: A. Automatically discarding commit history.
B. Allowing only the latest version to be visible.
C. Keeping track of the history of commits for reference.
D. Erasing all commit history for better performance.

questions.question: What additional directory does a Git repository have?
answers: A. .docs
B. .data
C. .info
D. .git

questions.question: What is the purpose of the .git directory in a Git repository?
answers: A. Storing user documentation.
B. Containing the actual project files.
C. Maintaining a mini-filesystem with versioning information.
D. Managing server synchronization.

questions.question: What role does the Git client play in managing the .git directory?
answers: A. Displaying commit history.
B. Optimizing the mini-filesystem.
C. Synchronizing with the server.
D. Creating and managing the .git directory.
